To find the maximum value of the expression \(\sqrt{abc} + \sqrt{(1 - a)(1 - b)(1 - c)}\) where \(0 \le a, b, c \le 1\), we start by considering the possible values of \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\).

1. If \(a = b = c = 0\), then the expression becomes \(\sqrt{0 \cdot 0 \cdot 0} + \sqrt{(1 - 0)(1 - 0)(1 - 0)} = 0 + 1 = 1\).

\sqrt{abc} + \sqrt{(1 - a)(1 - b)(1 - c)} \le \sqrt{abc + (1 - a)(1 - b)(1 - c)}.

abc + (1 - a)(1 - b)(1 - c) = abc + 1 - a - b - c + ab + bc + ca - abc = 1 - (a + b + c - ab - bc - ca).
